summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1815–1818), later serving as Professeur d’Arabe at INALCO (1838) and Conservateur at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1854).
Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.
Josho Nozawa (1907–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1950).

Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at Dalton School, Yale University (~1987–1991), the University of Oxford (~1991–1993), and Harvard University (~1993–1998). He held a post at Princeton University from 1998 to 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held an attested post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center in 2004.

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was a philosopher who studied at UC Berkeley (~1871–1875) and Johns Hopkins (~1876–1878). He held academic posts at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and Harvard University (~1882–1916).

José Ignacio Cabezón specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Caltech, Sera Jey Monastery, and UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he held posts at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (from 2001).
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and LMU Munich, she has held posts at UC Berkeley, Oxford, Munich, Heidelberg, Göttingen, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Joy Brennan works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, and studied with traditional teacher Diane Martin.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, she held posts at the University of Lille (~2000–2017) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2018).

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Western Washington University and with traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche. She became chair of Religious Studies at Naropa University in 1977.

Juhn Y. Ahn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007 and was attested in 2019 as an Associate Professor at the University of Michigan.
Juhyung Rhi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley and became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.

Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in religious studies who pursued postgraduate and PhD candidate studies at the University of Bradford (2000–2001, attested 2010). He also studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bourbon college and Lycée Louis-le-Grand, he held posts at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques (~1839–1895).

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at the University of Paris, INALCO, and EPHE, he taught at EPHE (1908–1914, 1919–1951), INALCO (1921–1937), Lyon (1941–1944), and held a chair at the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, founded the Light of Berotsana Translation Group (1999), and was an assistant professor at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was an historian who studied at the Lycée Charlemagne (1812–1816). He held posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1822), École Normale Supérieure (1827), Archives nationales (1830–1852), and Collège de France (1838–1852).
